sampling_model.design: Fixed-stratum superpopulation triangular arrays contain exactly \(n_{\mathcal R}\) randomized-trial records and \(n_{\mathcal E}\) external-control records; \(P_n\) is only the deterministic-fraction reference mixture.
sampling_model.units: Within each row the two strata are mutually independent, observations are independent within strata, and both deterministic stratum fractions stay bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is randomized only in the fixed trial stratum; every record in the fixed external stratum is observed under control and carries the observed tie breaker \(V\).
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment and reference-mixture trial-source propensities are uniformly bounded away from zero on the trial covariate support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A prespecified fold map selects learners whose existence and \(L_2\) rate are properties of the nuisance tuple; the displayed estimator evaluates those learners out of fold, while the anchor influence ranking is the exact full-trial empirical functional.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~2 gives \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) MSE estimation for any given borrowed set, and Theorem~3 gives selection consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive separation.
Theorem~1 gives asymptotic normality of a fixed-prefix estimator after centering by its prefix-specific bias.
Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

body.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion. Under a fixed-stratum triangular-array design, this project derives an exact all-prefix coupling for Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's selector and the correlated Gaussian-quadratic selected-ATE law across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps. A bounded no-covariate squared-loss construction gives two legal nested prefixes with exactly equal leading MSE but separated root-\(n\) ATE coordinates, so global exact-tie invariance fails and \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\). The remaining open content is the sharp excess modulus on empirically restricted prefix-Gram subclasses and a computable localized multiplier-projection interval with nominal coverage and modulus-calibrated length.

project_justification.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's Theorem~2 controls one given prefix, whereas their Theorem~3 selects a random prefix on a generated ranking; neither theorem supplies uniform expansion, the local quadratic argmin law, or post-selection ATE coverage at multiple minima. Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess settle analogous focused-selection inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem but not for generated individual ranks or a growing nested causal path.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a selector-specific modulus separating prefixes that are close in leading MSE from prefixes that are close as root-\(n\) ATE coordinates. The explicit legal witness shows that the unrestricted class has a positive exact-tie cost; useful adaptation therefore requires testable prefix-Gram localization.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the fixed-stratum all-prefix expansion and quadratic local law, establishes a legal tied-risk counterexample, and uses the resulting selection geometry to formulate nominal tie-uniform multiplier inference.

body.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the exact influence score in equation~(3), the nested top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1, the fixed-prefix bias and Gaussian expansion in Theorem~1, the pointwise MSE rate in Theorem~2, and fixed-gap selection consistency in Theorem~3; the proposed coupling is a strict simultaneous strengthening only of those stated fixed-prefix and given-ranking results. Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture, including the fact that local bias is not consistently estimable. Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess are the closest post-selection comparator: their Theorems~3 and~4 derive a focused-selector law and an interval allowing a prespecified worst-case coverage loss, but their candidate list is not generated by estimated individual ranks and their guarantee is not nominal uniformly over exact ties. Leeb and Poetscher establish the generic local impossibility that motivates the tied-risk witness. Fang and Santos show why ordinary resampling fails at nondifferentiable maps and how derivative-aware resampling can recover validity. Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo provide the regular-value derivative for sorting and classification operators; the edge-prefix lemma is needed because their compact-interior quantile analysis does not cover all top-\(k\) endpoints. Chernozhukov and coauthors provide cross-fitted orthogonal expansions, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike provide multiplier coupling for many correlated coordinates. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen and Zrnic and Fithian provide two complementary localization architectures for changing near-minimizer sets. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey provide conditional and hybrid inference for optimization-selected coordinates, but their selection variable is the target estimate itself rather than a generated quadratic MSE criterion. Zhu, Yang, and Wang obtain exact randomization-test validity for a sharp null and an excess-risk bound for conformal threshold borrowing; their design-based test is not a superpopulation confidence interval for the weak-null ATE selected by Yang's influence-ranked prefix rule.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The local-risk coordinate is the \(n\)-scaled MSE under \(n^{-1/2}\) exchangeability violations. Yang's squared bias estimate therefore retains first-order quadratic Gaussian noise. The regular coupling class imposes an interior score-margin condition, whereas the broader legal modulus class admits score atoms; the explicit witness belongs to the latter and need not satisfy the former. Exact finite-sample Fisher validity for a sharp null remains outside the superpopulation ATE target.
body.honest_scope: The fixed-stratum generated-prefix coupling and quadratic local law are theorem targets under the regular class. The explicit bounded squared-loss array is a theorem target showing that unrestricted exact-tie invariance fails. The sharp excess modulus on restricted prefix-Gram subclasses and the multiplier interval remain open; the interval must attain nominal coverage over the stated regular class. The no-borrowing corollary is an already-known sanity check and carries no novelty claim.
